claims: The Artemis II mission launches at approximately 17,000 mph (27,358 km/h).
The Artemis II mission accelerates to over 24,500 mph (39,400 km/h) to leave Earth's orbit for the Moon.
The Orion capsule hits Earth's atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h) upon returning.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket travels at roughly 17,000 mph.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket travels at 23 times the speed of sound.
The spacecraft reaches escape velocity of approx. 24,500–25,000 mph to leave Earth's orbit.
Approx. 24,500–25,000 mph is equivalent to 11 miles per second.
The Orion capsule strikes the atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h).
The heat shield must withstand temperatures of nearly 2,800°C during reentry.
Nearly 2,800°C is roughly half as hot as the Sun's surface.
Parachutes slow the capsule to approximately 17 mph (27 km/h) for a safe splashdown.
The Artemis II mission is designed to be the first crewed flight to the lunar vicinity since Apollo 17.
The Artemis II mission breaks records for the furthest distance humans have traveled from Earth.
